reader.requirement: At --std 85 every SPECIAL-NAMES clause of a containing program (implementor-name mnemonics, switch condition-names, ALPHABET, SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS, CLASS, CURRENCY SIGN, DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA) must apply to every directly or indirectly contained program, which itself may not write a Configuration Section, and the container's condition-names must be referenceable there.

reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f06_04 covers one level of containment; indirect containment, a mnemonic-name for a device, an alphabet used by a contained SORT, and the refusal of a contained Configuration Section are not exercised

probes.printed: C ED=# 12,50 / C VOWEL YES / C SYM=ZZ / C SW2 ON / C SORTED Z B A C

reader.notes: ConfigurationStep.Produce seeds a contained unit's slice from its container through Inherit, which copies the whole SPECIAL-NAMES-derived state; the container itself inherited first, so indirect containment works (sn1a, two levels). The contained-config refusal cites only 2023 text at 85 but the 1985 rule is the same.

refuter.evidence: r41a-001: container SPECIAL-NAMES (SWITCH-3 with ON/OFF condition-names, ALPHABET EB IS EBCDIC, SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS EBA IS 194 STAR IS 43, CLASS HEXD with THRU, DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA) applied to two SIBLING contained programs: R41B does SET SW3 TO ON and writes a sequential file with FD CODE-SET IS EB; R41C sees SW3-ON, VALUE STAR gives '**', VALUE 1,25 and PIC Z9,99 print ' 1,25', CLASS HEXD true for 'C'; the container then sees SW3 ON and reads back the byte as EBCDIC 'A' (= symbolic 194). Reader's sn1b covers the contained CONFIGURATION SECTION refusal. cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR1  (4.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1
